source_read: PDF, pp. 586–608 (all pages; Tables 1, 2 and 4 checked on rendered pages)

anchors.locator: Methamphetamine Neuropharmacology, last paragraph (begins on p. 588; the cited sentences are on p. 589)
anchors.note: Large bolus doses to drug-naive animals; prior escalating doses prevented the effects of later large doses (Segal et al., 2003; O'Neil et al., 2006; Belcher et al., 2008).

anchors.locator: Review of the Acute Effects (pp. 589–592); Table 1 (pp. 590–591); Conclusions, 1st paragraph (p. 604)
anchors.extracted: Table 1 lists 16 controlled laboratory studies with doses up to 50 mg/70 kg intranasal, 30 mg intravenous and 40 mg oral (study conditions). None is scored as worsening a domain and most show improvement in some (visuospatial perception, sustained attention or vigilance, response speed). Not all gave single doses: Comer et al. (2001) is titled as a repeated oral administration study (reference list, p. 606). In Silber et al. (2006) d-methamphetamine was worse than placebo on visuospatial processing in a first session, scored as no effect (p. 591). What was not tested is larger doses given repeatedly (pp. 592, 604).
anchors.note: The editors' count of 16 is correct (11 on p. 590, 5 on p. 591). For Hart et al. (2008) the text says sustained attention improved (p. 592) while Table 1 lists vigilance improved and sustained attention unchanged (p. 590).

anchors.locator: Main text: McCann et al. (2008) comparison (p. 596, right column); Simon et al. (2002) comparison (p. 602, right column)
anchors.note: Factual basis confirmed: the McCann comparison takes two sentences and the Simon comparison one, and neither gives the norms, cut-offs or values used. The second half of the anchor is the editors' appraisal; the review's own account of Kalechstein et al. (2003, p. 602) shows a minority of users meeting an individual criterion.

anchors.locator: Right column, last paragraph before 'PET studies investigating brain metabolism'

for_senior_author: Interpretation gap: reader 2 rates it moderate rather than minor (the conclusions move from not established to not supported by evidence and to concerns being unwarranted, p. 605; the abstract's 'overwhelmingly within the normal range' rests on a few unreported normative comparisons of group means). Card unchanged; reader 2 rated Dean et al. (2013) moderate as well, for consistency.
not_added: Key finding 8: the metabolism-paper row of Table 2 (p. 595) also describes the thalamic and striatal decreases without saying they were normalized values: confirmed; not added (covered on the Volkow 2001c card).
